stopped_because: ran the 5 iterations it was given
policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red, blue or green); call it the goal cube. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a time marker; which side of it matters is set by the goal's word 'before' or 'after', and goal_target in memory already encodes that choice, so the drop point always follows the memory. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, goal_target unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): first read whether the goal says 'right before' or 'right after' the button was pressed, compute goal_target from the demonstration as the memory instruction says (the physical target the chosen placement landed on, followed through any movement of targets in the final demonstration frames, then mapped to the execution scene), then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to goal_target, which already accounts for any target movement in the demonstration, so never re-derive the drop point from where the placement visually happened (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [127, 146]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of goal_target (it may be hidden), point at goal_target itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and goal_target is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on goal_target: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.

fields.name: cube_placed
fields.description: 'no' at the first step and at every step until the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to ~100% while the gripper height is under 0.05 and the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of goal_target; from that step on write 'yes'. e.g. no

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is empty (first step, demonstration shown): first read the goal instruction and note whether it says 'right before' or 'right after' the button was pressed. Then in the demonstration steps find the press: the first frame with fingers 0% open where the gripper is low (height under 0.08) over the button and the button's y jumps a few pixels. List the placements: frames where the fingers go from ~46% to at least ~95% open with height under 0.05 and the cube in that frame lies within about 8 pixels of a listed target (a release with no target within about 10 pixels of the cube is a drop on bare table; ignore it). For 'before', take the last placement earlier than the press; for 'after', take the first placement later than the press. Note the listed target nearest the cube in that placement frame; that is the physical target the cube was placed on. Follow that same target forward through every remaining demonstration frame, matching entries from one frame to the next by nearest position (it may drift a few pixels, vanish while occluded, and in the final frames with the gripper parked at height 0.200 the targets may move tens of pixels per frame or swap places; keep following the one you started with, do not switch to whichever entry is nearest the original spot). Among the target entries in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, write the [y, x] of the one nearest the followed target's position in the last demonstration frame. If no target moved after the placement, this is the execution-scene target nearest the placement spot. e.g. [86, 100]
